title: Proposal
description: The mutation queue for the conserved core. Changing the spec, a standard, an authority grant, a schema, or an autonomy policy is not an ordinary edit: it goes through a Proposal that states the reason, the evidence, the expected benefit, how the change will be validated, and how it is rolled back. A Proposal reaching a terminal status carries a Ruling with the decider's canonical ID and their words verbatim.

id.description: Canonical, permanent proposal ID. Numbers are never reused, including for withdrawn proposals.

status.description: 'accepted' means ruled on but not yet landed. 'applied' means the conserved files now reflect it.

author.description: Who wrote the proposal. Agents may author freely; authorship carries no authority.

targets.description: The conserved surfaces this proposal mutates. Anything not listed here is out of scope for the ruling.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the conserved file.

change.description: One line on what changes in this file.

reason.description: The friction that forced this proposal. Not the solution.

evidence.description: What makes the reason a fact rather than an opinion: incident IDs, audit references, failing runs, dated observations.

validation.description: How anyone will know afterwards whether the change worked. A proposal with no falsifiable validation is a preference.

rollback.description: How the change is undone, and what is lost by undoing it.

ruling.description: The recorded exercise of authority. Required for every terminal status. A ruling claimed anywhere other than here is not a ruling.

actor.description: Rulings are made by humans. An agent may draft the wording; it may not be the actor.

verbatim.description: The decider's own words, quoted, not paraphrased.

adr.description: Repo-relative path of the ADR recording the change, when the change is architectural.

supersededBy.description: The proposal that replaced this one. Required when status is 'superseded'.
